name: John
overview: John, a male fisherman and one of the Twelve apostles, is identified as the son of Zebedee. He is noted for mending nets and was called by Jesus to follow Him. John is also recognized as the author of the book of John.
namesAndTitles: The proper name John means 'YHVH is gracious,' reflecting the Hebrew origin of the name. He was given the title 'Son of thunder,' meaning 'son of a noisy crowd,' which was a divine designation. Additionally, he is called 'The Elder,' a title indicating age and respect, though not given by God.
familyAndRelationships: John is the son of Zebedee and the brother of James. He is a disciple and apostle of YHVH, indicating his close relationship with Jesus Christ. These relationships are explicitly recorded in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: John holds a significant place in the biblical narrative as a key member of Jesus' inner circle and one of the Twelve apostles. His role as a trusted disciple is underscored by his presence at major events and his care for Mary at the crucifixion. As the author of the Gospel of John, his writings deeply reveal the deity of Christ and emphasize a personal, loving relationship with Him, providing profound theological insight.
